text: Hey guys, it's Joanne from 15 Spatulas, and today we're going to make New England style clam chowder.
This is a cream-based chowder instead of the tomato-based Manhattan-style chowder.
I just think the cream-based tastes so much better.
But I don't claim this to be an authentic New England clam chowder.
There's all sorts of arguments about what that even means,
because there's so many ways that people make New England clam chowder.
But for my version, there's two things that I like to do.
First of all, I love using fresh clams.
I think it just tastes so much better.

and I haven't found a brand that I think really tastes good.
And then the second thing is, this isn't a flour-thickened soup.
I think sometimes New England clam chowders can be kind of gloopy and thick, if you know what I mean.

Start by rinsing two dozen little...
...little neck clams, making sure to wash off any mud or sand from the outside.
And then put them in a bowl and top with cold water.
And let the clams soak for about 30 minutes so they can spit out any sand from the inside.
In the meantime, chop up one large yellow onion.
You want to end up with about two cups total for this.
And when the clams are done, rinse off the clams again.
